Detailed Case Study Results The following sections provide more detailed summaries of transmission project case studies. C.1 MISO Multi-Value Project Planning Portfolio MISO’s approach to multivalue planning and cost allocation is based on the philosophy that the benefits of transmission will change over time but coordination among states to deploy regional transmission infrastructure will ensure broad-based shared benefits (Doner 2023). The MISO Multi-Value Project (MVP) portfolio includes 17 projects identified through MISO’s 2011 Transmission Expansion Plan (MTEP 11) (MISO 2011). The MVP portfolios were originally championed by the governors of Minnesota, Iowa, Wisconsin, North Dakota, and South Dakota interested in transmission development to enable increased generator interconnection toward their respective state policy mandates. In 2008, these governors announced the creation of the Upper Midwest Transmission Development Initiative to identify wind generation resources and necessary transmission infrastructure (State of Minnesota 2008). The initiative would also develop a cost allocation proposal for the new transmission to propose to MISO and contribute alongside state public utility commissions and the Organization of MISO States to MISO’s analysis of wind energy in the region as part of the “Regional Generation Outlet Study” published in 2010 (MISO 2010).
